I bought the first case in August of '18, and was well pleased with the product. Last week, I was moving some stuff out of my vehicle's front seat to the back. I laid my Samsung Tab A on the roof. Friends arrived and we left, heading out a four lane where the speed limit is 50MPH. As I accelerated, I heard a bump, but didn't miss my tablet. Thirty minutes later, I missed the tablet and drove back to the section where I heard the bump. After five minutes, I saw the tablet in a turnout lane. I was happy to find it, thinking I could transfer files to my new tablet that I was certain that I would need. To my amazement, the screen was not cracked. I powered it up, and there were no issues. The case was scuffed and there were dings on the screen protector. So I figure the screen would reflect this. When I opened the case, the screen was perfect. The case and screen protector completely saved my tablet. This is how you make customers for life- a good product at a good price. My new case arrived and now I am once again protected against my own stupidity.

ArmorSuit MilitaryShield Screen Protector for Apple iPad Mini 1/2/3 - [Max Coverage] Anti-Bubble HD Clear Film I really can't say enough good things about this, especially at the price I paid on Amazon.

I'm VERY very very OCD about my screen protectors, and the unique wet application of this one makes it an absolute joy to apply and to use.

The instructions are very easy to follow, all you need is in the kit.

So you spray the spray stuff on, slide the shield around until it's where you want it, then squeegee it down and let it sit. For me, the iPad was completely useable immediately.

What's even better is, a few months later, the corners were lifting and getting some grit under them (not a flaw in the shield ... I was using this with an iPad cover whose silicone covers move a little and shove the shield up). I pulled the corners up, sprayed the solution on (they send way more than you need for one application), flicked off the grit, squeegeed it back down ... good as new!

Given the flexible nature of the film I think a lot of devices that get a lot of rubbing at the edges might get this peeling effect, but it's great how keeping that bottle of spray around lets you fix it right up. When I peeled the corner back i accidentally touched some tissue to the guard, and it stuck to it, and I thought I was done for ... but spraying the liquid solution on, the tissue let go and like I said, it went back down at the corners as good as new.

I'll absolutely be buying these for all future big electronic purchases.
text_fidelity_b: ArmorSuit MilitaryShield Screen Protector for Apple iPad Mini 1/2/3 - [Max Coverage] Anti-Bubble HD Clear Film

text_fidelity_a:
Case Logic MSEC-2 EVA Molded Compact Camera Case (Blue) Don't expect this case to be a hard shell case. It's certainly harder than the soft, padded cases but it can be easily bent back and forth with little pressure. There is no padding on the inside so therefore nothing but the case shell and your camera to absorb shock if it's dropped. I wouldn't feel particularly good about dropping my camera while inside this case, but it would be better than no case at all.

Despite the shell of the case being made of plastic, it is not waterproof since water can seep in around and through the zipper which begins at the bottom of the case and goes all the way around back to the bottom again. There is a mesh pouch on the inside of the case but I find little room is left after my regular sized digital camera is placed inside the case to have much space left for something to be placed in the mesh pouch. I don't think the pouch will hold much except for maybe very flat items such as an extra card or flat battery. I can't close the case with my camera (Fuji EXR) and 2 AA batteries inside. I have to take the batteries out. It won't hold a Flip recorder or any camera bigger than a flat digital.

I don't understand the nonadjustable lanyard either. I don't want to wear this case around my neck and there is no way to secure it onto a belt or belt loops. And it's not all that easy to quickly get your camera out when you need to take a fast picture and even more difficult to put it back into it's case. It always takes two hands. At least it won't fall all the way open because it has a an elastic strap on both sides (secured from the inside) to prevent it from opening up completely. Your camera isn't likely to fall out immediately but will eventually if you don't close it back up.

Nice color though....I really like the deep ocean blue color.
text_fidelity_b: Case Logic MSEC-2 EVA Molded Compact Camera Case (Blue)

text_fidelity_a:
KINESIS Freestyle2 USB Keyboard for Mac (9" Standard Separation), Black Overall this keyboard is great. The keys feel nice and they're quiet but not too quiet or soft or squishy. Enjoy typing on this keyboard, pushing the keys seems to take minimal effort and overall it's great.

The best part about the keyboard is that it separates and having the ability to give it a little separation is great. I miss it when I don't have it and it helps avoid torquing the wrists when you are typing. I also love the feel of the keys.

Now before my minor complaints understand two things: (1) I really like this keyboard and despite what I would consider minor defects, I would definitely buy another one. (2) please excuse the fact that I like my keyboards to be consistent and while Apple may not make the *best* keyboards I do use a laptop and I am used to their keyboard layout and feel.

The biggest thing that annoyed me when I purchased this keyboard was the positioning of the ⌘ (command) key. It seems to be shifted over a bit from what I'm used to. Normally I would hit ⌘ with my thumb but it's a little touch to do that on this one given the position of it. It's just something I'm having to get used to.

One minor downside to the keyboard is that the function key doesn't work the same way as the default apple keyboard, rather, the `fn` key is a toggle. I prefer for fn to work as a modifier because that is what I am used to on my laptop keyboard.

Another minor problem is the styling on the caps lock key. Like many people, I remap my caps lock to ctrl and and thus want caps lock to be a normal button. However, on this keyboard the caps lock key is missing the right part of the key so that you don't accidentally hit it when typing the `a` key.

Finally, the escape key and '`' (back tick) keys are in weird positions. The escape key is not as bad as the backtick. There is just something about the distance that I must go that is different from what I'm used to and I have been consistently hitting the `1` key instead. Life goes on.
text_fidelity_b: KINESIS Freestyle2 USB Keyboard for Mac (9" Standard Separation), Black

text_fidelity_a:
SiriusXM Onyx Plus Satellite Radio w/ Vehicle Kit, Enjoy SiriusXM Through your Existing Car Stereo for as Low as $5/month + $60 Service Card with Activation So let's start out with that it's a nice step up from your standard car radio. I like the overall design and you can save up to 20 channels and have 5 saved stations that you can tune into to transmit your signal, which I find nice for those areas when you start picking up other radio stations and there is bleed through. I didn't realize this at first, but the radio does have an internal transmitter, though I don't know if having it directly plugged into a transmitter will make any difference. So far mine has done nicely without the help of a third party transmitter. The little screen is nice too. It is not a touch screen, but you can see it well during the daytime and I find that for me the brightness at night is just right, not super blinding bright, but not so dim that you can't see it either. The radio also works similar to DVR and you can rewind to play a song again.

Set up is fairly easy and the instructions are easy to follow as well. I'd say it may take 30 minutes to an hour tops to set it up (that includes tucking away cords and positioning it where you want it) and activating it.

It does not come with a remote, but I think it would improve the experience of going through the channels, especially when driving, so you can still keep your eyes on the road and change the channel if you are wanting something different from your presets. Also, I believe you have to have a Sirius dock/boom box of sorts if you want to bring it inside and play music. You can transfer this radio between cars too, depending on your setup though, you may want to have a secondary dock and antenna set up in the second vehicle so its easier to transition and your not having to drag the dock and accessories around from car to car.

Something to take into consideration if you are thinking of getting this radio or other xm radios is that if you are not familiar with the subscription charges, is that you will have to pay the subscription fee, your state tax and a royalty fee and there is an activation fee. So outside of tax, I didn't realize there were other charges with the subscription fee. Personally I went with the 10.99 subscription and my fees were estimated to be 14.99 (this will probably vary from location to location), so not too much extra on regular fees after the activation fee. Just something to know so your not caught by surprise.

If its really cloudy or if you are under something like a metal awning/covering, the signal will go out.

I think the only thing that I don't like about the radio is the antenna. The reason I don't like the antenna is because the cord is too long for how I use it. I keep the antenna inside my car and the signal works fine, but the cord is ridiculously long. It could be upgraded to a motorcycle antenna, which is about 8 inches long, compared to X amount of feet. For others this won't be a problem, because you may need every bit of that extra cord, so it just depends on how you plan to set it up.
text_fidelity_b: SiriusXM Onyx Plus Satellite Radio w/ Vehicle Kit, Enjoy SiriusXM Through your Existing Car Stereo for as Low as $5/month + $60 Service Card with Activation

text_fidelity_a: SamData 32GB USB Flash Drives 4 Pack 32GB Thumb Drives Memory Stick Jump Drive with LED Light for Storage and Backup (4 Colors: Black Blue Green Purple) This unit does work, but it is too slow for me to recommend it to others. When writing music onto it from my Windows computer, the write speed was slow enough to repeatedly drop the data transfer rate all the way to zero. Other manufacturers' flash drives do not do that; they keep on going. The read speed is slow enough that it causes my car's infotainment system (2019 model year) to sometimes hang up. Indeed, at one point, it caused my backup camera to go to all black for a minute or two. Note that some other reviewers are apparently unware of what flash memory is like. It has a limited number of times that it can be written (rewritten), and it will wear out if you try to use it as a substitute for a SSD. It also isn't going to be nearly as fast as a SSD. Flash memory is most appropriate for putting mp3 files into your car's infotainment system and other applications that are write only a few times but read many times.
text_fidelity_b: SamData 32GB USB Flash Drives 4 Pack 32GB Thumb Drives Memory Stick Jump Drive with LED Light for Storage and Backup (4 Colors: Black Blue Green Purple)

Jaybird X2 Sport Wireless Bluetooth Headphones - Midnight Black Finally seem to have found a pair of bluetooth headphones with acceptable connection performance. I was begining to think that it was too much to ask to be able to put my phone in my pocket and still be connected. Or to walk more than a few feet away from my phone and still stay connected. These ace those tests. Connectivity is not perfect but I am willing to accept that as it's bluetooth. I do get the occasional drop for no apparent reason but it is not often enough to be a huge negative.
They come packaged really nicely. So nicely you almost feel obligated to go slow and enjoy the experience.
You have to chose between the silicone or foam ear bud tips. The silicone feels softer and goes in and out easier. The foam will give you a more secure fit and sound isolation. I went with the foam and they do a fairly good job of keeping the outside world out. They are by no means 100 percent effective though.
I used the medium foam tips as well as the ear wings and find the comfort pretty good and the fit very secure. Wearing them for a couple hours was not an issue and I had no discomfort.
I cannot comment on their ability to transmit music as I use them for podcasts. Sound quality was fine for speech.
These have come down in price so much lately that I think they are a no brainer compared to the competition.
I dropped them a star due to the occasional random connection failure but overall I am very pleased with them.
text_fidelity_b: Jaybird X2 Sport Wireless Bluetooth Headphones - Midnight Black

text_fidelity_a:
MOSISO Fashion Laptop Backpack for Women, Pure Deep Gray I am in love with this bag!
It has so many features that are important to me.
I plan on using this bag for day trips with the family and especially during my childrens' swim meets.
This bag has more compartments and zippers then I expected it to have.
There are three main large compartments, two small compartments in the front and an anti-theft pocket in the back and the side water bottle mesh are also contained in a pocket. I was a little worried that I wouldn't be able to fit my water bottle in the outside mesh since there is a zipper and extra fabric and stuff, but as you can see from my image, a sports drink bottle fits perfectly in there.
The bag comes with its own lock which can be programmed to your own code.
The bag has two padded sections within the two largest zippered areas. One for a laptop with a velcro strip and one in the middle section with no velcro.
I plan to use the middle padded area for my mp3 player as this is the area that the headphone cables enter into and I will also put my power bank in that padded area since this is also where the charger port comes from.
The color of this bag is very modern, it's a good bag for a male or female.
I like that I can zip shut the drink compartments if I wanted to have something in them that I don't want to fall out (skittles/sunflower seeds)!
There is a padded carry handle and a non-padded hanging handle which is really nice. The back is very padded as are the shoulder straps.
There is even a luggage strap for if I wanted to bring this on the plane trip.
There are two cinch straps above each water bottle which is nice, as sometimes I like to cinch in my jacket or if I had a lot of bulky stuff inside that could be cinched to remove air and the bulk.
The bag has the interior organization in the front large compartment, including a clip for your keys, two wider sections, mesh on one and two pencil holes, which is great for me as I like to bring a pencil, sharpie, and highlighter with me to the swim meets.
I like that there are so many large compartments, allowing me to keep my stuff separate. I like to bring magazines to read between heats and sometimes my laptop (rear), snacks in the middle and the schedule and journal in the front.
I like the smaller compartment to contain the emergency kit (bandaids, pain reliever, etc).
I don't think there is anything else in a bag that this bag doesn't have.
A great mom bag!
text_fidelity_b: MOSISO Fashion Laptop Backpack for Women, Pure Deep Gray

Not wanting my new phone to be damaged over a cable I purchased on Amazon, I replaced the charging cable with another one from the pack.

As insane as it sounds, I had to charge my brick charger with this ridiculous cord, while the brick charged my phone (see picture) with the original brick charger cable. text_fidelity_a:
Bluetooth Earbuds,Kurdene Wireless Earbuds with Wireless Charging case,Touch Control in Ear Bluetooth 5.0 Waterproof Headphones CVC 8.0 Noise Cancelling Earphones with Deep Bass Sound for Sports(Pink) Pros

1. Excellent sound, with more clarity than the other Bluetooth earbuds I own. They are especially better for listening to music.

2. The earbuds and their case have a sleek, attractive design.

Cons

1. Each small ear piece operates separately. They are not attached to each other via a plastic-coated wire as is typically the case for earbuds. This means that, when I remove these earbuds from my ears, because there is no wire holding them securely around my neck, they must be carefully and consistently placed in their carrying case, and then either set in a safe, easily remembered location, or placed in my pants pocket. Neither option is desirable. It is extremely difficult to not get distracted and set down these earbuds in a random location, such that afterwards I have to waste a lot of time looking for them. And the problem with slipping them into a pocket is that there is a strong possibility I might accidentally leave them there, such that they end up in the washer and dryer and are ruined. In short, the risk of losing or destroying these earbuds is enormous!

2. Each ear piece must be turned ON/OFF separately, one after the other. This is a hassle.

3. The ON/OFF controls are extremely difficult to engage. You touch an ear piece and hold it for several seconds to turn each ear piece on or off. There is no button. The ear piece is somehow sensing the pressure of the touch of a fingertip. I frequently have great difficulty locating and pressing the exact spot required in order to turn these earbuds on or off. This is a major pain!

4. Volume is controlled the same way as the ON/OFF function, by magically managing to touch the earpiece in the exact, necessary location with the appropriate amount of fingertip pressure. It is very difficult to accomplish that, and the frustration of failing at this onerous task again and again is maddening!

For all of the above reasons, I wouldn’t recommend these earbuds to my worst enemy!
text_fidelity_b: Bluetooth Earbuds,Kurdene Wireless Earbuds with Wireless Charging case,Touch Control in Ear Bluetooth 5.0 Waterproof Headphones CVC 8.0 Noise Cancelling Earphones with Deep Bass Sound for Sports(Pink)

text_fidelity_a:
JVC HARX700 Precision Sound Full Size Headphones - Black ~Comfortable for hours. These are light years ahead of earbuds, on ear, or over ear phones. No part of my ear was pinched or scrunched, even though I wear glasses. I have an over-sized melon and large, flat ears. I can't tolerate buds for more than about 30 minutes, and most headphones in this range are pinchy somewhere.
~I normally watch movies/videos at full sound with Closed Caption on iPad or laptops. I'm at half volume -- no CC -- wearing these phones. I was able to easily pick up male and female voices, including foreign accents.
~NOT noise cancelling. I could still hear the whir of a fan, my kids talking, etc., but they couldn't hear any noise coming from my headphones. For me, this was ideal. I don't have the luxury of tuning out the world most of the time.
~Requires several hours of break-in. I usually listen to Winterspell from Two Steps to test buds and phones. It sounded tinny on first listen, and amazing about 10 hours in.
I highly recommend these if you have moderate hearing loss. I can't differentiate consonant sounds, and certain voices and accents are nearly impossible for me to follow on screen. These didn't feel loud, just incredibly clear -- it was like hearing like a kid again.
text_fidelity_b: JVC HARX700 Precision Sound Full Size Headphones - Black

We had one with a long antenna in our wishlist for a year or more. We have, I would say, a middle class income, and only my husband works. The antenna he had finally started to really not work well and as I was going to purchase it (it would have been $22) he asked me to look for the low profile version. He runs local and is home every night, but still, 16 hours a day in a truck, I want him to be happy. His Sirius radio makes him happy.

He installed this in about 15 minutes and the cabling goes in through a small waterproof port above his window that was already there. He drives a pneumatic bulk tanker daycab. The connection to his mirror is very secure. It is not a big ole antenna that says HERE I AM. It is very subdued.

Did he notice a difference? Yes! Not only does the sound now not break up because the wire on the old one was bad ... but THIS one seems to be more clear and does not lose signal at all. He pretty much just has an uninterrupted stream of music and news and whatever.

Very happy with our purchase and no complaints at all.

Yamaha Audio SR-C20A Compact Sound Bar with Built-in Subwoofer and Bluetooth This SR-C20A is an entry-level Yamaha soundbar made for the smaller room and bedroom. The attraction to this model was the 3rd speaker, a powered subwoofer.

Most compact soundbars create bass through passive radiators integral with the bar … i.e. 2 powered speakers separated in width by a baffled tube radiating through holes. So, there is no controllable bass other than passive baffle sound effects.

The SR-C20A has a controllable powered subwoofer and a dual baffle radiator combined to deliver controllable high, medium, and low tones. There are five modes: standard, stereo, game, movie, and a virtual surround mode. I just picked the one that sounds best. The virtual surround provides a sense of depth and separation to my hearing.

The SR-C20A soundbar replaced a no-name 2-speaker with baffles. The difference is sizable sound improvement.

Easy install, lots of input options.

Better sound than expected. Impressive sound. Sized for the smaller room LCD/OLEAD TV. Priced right.
text_fidelity_b: Yamaha Audio SR-C20A Compact Sound Bar with Built-in Subwoofer and Bluetooth

Kindle Paperwhite E-reader (Previous Generation - 7th) - Black, 6" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi) with Built-in Light, Wi-Fi + Free Cellular Connectivity - Includes Special Offers For years, I used the keyboard kindle after it first came out and loved the "classic" look of the page so much. After replacing it several times due to screen issues, I finally made the switch to the paperwhite with some skepticism, thinking the back-light would make it into yet another screen I look at. I was pleasantly surprised that even the brighter settings still look like a page, and I can turn it all the way down for the same effect as my older model kindle. Plus, I don't need to bother anyone with a light anymore when I read in bed, in the car at night, etc.

Paying a bit extra for no ads was worth it, and I enjoy the drawings that serve as screensavers. The home page is not my favorite - I would prefer to default to my library list instead of wading through recommendations, etc. - but it's not that much of a hassle to tap over to the library screen. When I'm reading a book, it automatically opens to the page I left off on just like my old kindle.

I only vaguely miss having the 3G function my old kindle had because I used to live out in the boonies with limited internet access. However, the WiFi has been generally sufficient and now I just make sure I download a few books before I travel.

Overall, the kindle has definitely revolutionized the way I read since it first came out when I was in high school. I do still keep a lot of hard copies of my favorite series and enjoy reading real books from time to time, but the kindle is SO easy to download anything, anytime you want. Not to mention bringing a whole library with you in one slim package while traveling! I have had this model for a year and a half now, and have no issues or complaints at this time.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Paperwhite E-reader (Previous Generation - 7th) - Black, 6" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi) with Built-in Light, Wi-Fi + Free Cellular Connectivity - Includes Special Offers

text_fidelity_a: Google WiFi system, 3-Pack - Router Replacement for Whole Home Coverage (NLS-1304-25),White Easy to setup and works like a charm @ first. Until it didn't. O.k. I must say I know enough about mesh networks to be dangerous but I must say something from the very beginning with the mesh system was strange. Alright it all started back at the beginning of the year where at certain times of night my internet would drag. I said, "NIGHT." Typically in the morning when everyone else is sleep. I am up working. I would notice download speeds of maybe about 25 and uploads at 10. So after a few days of this,  I contacted Xfinity internet support and ask them to run a check on the internet. Right away, the support guy said, "Log into your account and let me show you something."  I said O.k. and right there I am seeing the traffic go thru the roof. The rep said, "Oh yes there is a lot of traffic on for some reason coming from Somalia. I said are you sure. He said Oh yes.  Since I run a business I have backup internet thru another company that I can jump on in case my internet goes down.  So I disconnected my internet and and change the wifi mesh name and password. Later that morning, I noticed that the ssid was still broadcasting my old ssid name so I connected too it and noticed that I still had internet.  REALLY!!!!! I could watch movies and everything. Very strange. So I contacted Google support and was told to reset the mesh back to the original factory systems. Now for the last 4 to 5 months I have to change my ssid every few months and reset everything back to factory settings to keep my internet from dragging. I haven't read anything else about this expect a few bloggers and you-tubers say that they suspect that the mesh network can be hacked.  I must say after a few months of tracking my internet usage online I must say I suspect the same. If you purchase this check your usage regularly.  I have owned this mesh system since 2017 and didn't notice any problems until recently. Trying a new mesh network. It think it is time.
text_fidelity_b: Google WiFi system, 3-Pack - Router Replacement for Whole Home Coverage (NLS-1304-25),White

ByronStatics Record Player, Vinyl Turntable Records Player Bluetooth 5.0, Built in Stereo Speakers, 3 Speed, Extra Stylus, Supports RCA Line Out, AUX in, Portable Suitcase Record Player - Dark Grey This record player is mostly my husbands. We listen to very different music. He's more Zeppelin, I'm more not. However, we both have our vinyls. This one is portable so he can use it wherever his little heart desires. I asked him to give me a few words about it after he used it for a bit and here is what he had to say about it:

"This is very attractive in the form of a suitcase with a neat clasp to keep your record player safe. Plus it's a record player and to this day vinyl is better than everything else, especially digital.
It has Bluetooth and a headphone jack. It can play your records and has an automatic stop. All this stuff is great and I want to really like this. Alas, there are some drawbacks. Firstly, and not of major importance to me personally, the Bluetooth has a bit of trouble connecting. I was trying to connect to a Google pixel 3 and though it does create a connection that's about all it does.
Secondly, the speakers really aren't all that good. The test of this was with Zeppelin 2 playing and when it just doesn't do John Paul Jones any justice then it just doesn't cut it.
You need to add speakers or get it connecting to something with a decent sound because no, just no.
I left it at a three because instead of being a really good record player it sort of turned into a half decent novelty item. For the price I can't really complain too much but if you really want to hear vinyl then try another record player."

There you have it folks. His opinion on the player. I will say one thing though. He's not really good with connecting Bluetooth devices so take that part of his review with a grain of salt. I tried to tell him to attempt to connect one of the little Bluetooth speaker things we have all over but he just wanted to try it on his phone. So I would check other reviews and see what others say about that first, just in case. Other than that the rest is pretty much how he feels and stuff. So, there you have it!
text_fidelity_b: ByronStatics Record Player, Vinyl Turntable Records Player Bluetooth 5.0, Built in Stereo Speakers, 3 Speed, Extra Stylus, Supports RCA Line Out, AUX in, Portable Suitcase Record Player - Dark Grey

It touts the ability to take 3D pictures and underwater capabilities (though I've not tested either). Compared to the pricier [[ASIN:B006K552V6 Sony Cyber-shot DSC-TX66 18.2 MP Exmor R CMOS Digital Camera with 5x Optical Zoom and 3.3-inch OLED (White) (2012 Model)]], this one provides more zoom; however the pricier DSC-TX66 provides a touch-screen control (OLED display) and is much thinner and lighter. Having used to the touch-screen controls of TX66, the scroll-based menu in the WX150 seems less impressive - however, the controls on both are very intuitive - given the wide range of options, it will take some time to get used to all the command settings. The video quality of both cameras are exceptional - and either will replace a handycam easily. If you are more interested in a lighter camera with a touch screen and willing to compromise on the zoom (5X opposed to 10X in the WX150) and pay up for it (about 100$ more), DSC-TX66 may be a better choice. But if the touchscreen is not a critical requirement for you and zoom is of more importance, WX150 is a very compelling choice at this price-point. The DSLR-like quality with a very respectable zoom, plethora of picture settings options, and fairly intuitive scroll-based menus makes this a good value.
text_fidelity_b: Sony Cyber-shot DSC-WX150 18.2 MP Exmor R CMOS Digital Camera with 10x Optical Zoom and 3.0-inch LCD (Silver) (2012 Model)

text_fidelity_a:
SAMSUNG Galaxy Buds Live True Wireless Bluetooth Earbuds w/ Active Noise Cancelling, Charging Case, AKG Tuned 12mm Speaker, Long Battery Life, US Version, Mystic Red I bought mine direct from Samsung and ultimately returned them. I found that I had to fiddle with them constantly to hit the sweet spot for the music to sound like it should instead of like I was listening through a tin can, and while fiddling with them the touch controls become an annoying hassle because you are trying to get the fit right and the music is turning on and off and pausing and skipping, etc, because you are touching them. The buds can't seem to differentiate at all between an actual hold/grip to manipulate them in your ears, and a tap as you would do to actually use a touch control feature.

Don't quote me on this because it's not like I counted every review that appeared male vs female, but I found that they hurt and I think it might be because they were designed by somewhat larger-eared males. I originally assumed the hurty issue was likely because they were designed by some 60 year old man engineer with huge ears (because ears grow our whole lives) and so they were only made to fit kind of older larger ears. I even wrote on my Samsung review that they should have made the fit for the age group of their customer. But now, reading these Amazon reviews, I am noticing that the people saying they fit great seem to mostly be male names and those saying they hurt seem to mostly be female-normative names, so I still think they were designed for larger ears, but maybe for males they will fit better - I truly don't know how different in size male vs female ears are though; it's just a random observation of these reviews of hurt vs feel great.

Bottom line, they hurt my ears and were too picky about being perfectly aligned in my ear. On the rare occasion I hit that sweet spot they sounded great and never felt like they were going to fall out. Too bad it took so much effort to find that spot.
text_fidelity_b: SAMSUNG Galaxy Buds Live True Wireless Bluetooth Earbuds w/ Active Noise Cancelling, Charging Case, AKG Tuned 12mm Speaker, Long Battery Life, US Version, Mystic Red

So - it has essentially been the following cycle: would not take charge -- repair (2 weeks) - would take charge for a day, then would not take charge - - repair (2 weeks) - would take charge for a day, then would not take charge - - repair (2 weeks) - would take charge for a day, then would not take charge - then I finally decided to call customer service again, but demanding refund, being fed up with this whole brand altogether. Datacolor Spyder5EXPRESS – Designed for Hobbyist Photographers (S5X100) I ended up using this colorimeter to profile and calibrate my monitor. Out of the box I was not very happy with the quality of the product. You end up getting pretty much zero instruction and no manual. I had to figure it out on my own just by looking at the product. Once that annoyance was over I got to experience how terrible the default software from datacolor is.

I looked to the reviews and decided I could make the most of this purchase by using other free calibration software. I used Argyll and DispCalGUI. If you simply download DispCalGUI it will prompt you automatically to download the Argyll color libraries.

You then go into Tools->Instrument->install Argyll CMS instrument drivers...

This will download the drivers you need to run the spyder 5.

After this calibration is possible. I calibrated and it seemed to do a decent job. All in all, the calibration software looked like it was powerful--certainly better than the default.

In the end, I returned the product. I wanted something that would work without me having to go the extra mile to get it to work. At this point, with all of the extra I had to do to calibrate I still don't know if it did a good job or not.

Dimensions can be seen in the photos I have attached.

Included is the unit only.

Pros:
*Calibrates
*Decent price

Cons:
*Terrible OEM software (-2 stars)
*Setup--while not hard--is not immediately obvious. A small pamphlet would have gone a long way (-1/2 a star)

Additional Considerations:
Go for hardware that has good software calibration tools. You cant beat the two working in synergy.

Overall: 2.5/5 stars (>=.5 rounds up, <.5 rounds down) => 3 stars

If you have any further questions regarding the product in my review please leave a comment below and I will get back to you as soon as possible.

ContourROAM Hands-free HD Camcorder Picked up a couple of these when Amazon had them on sale for half price. Had to return one because it was out of focus; Amazon processed the return quickly and the replacement works great.

Very pleased with the image quality of these cameras in the 1080p mode (which I always use). The video quality is sharp and colorful. Make sure you use the camera software to set the image quality to the highest level for best results.

Sound quality is a mixed bag. This camera uses noise reduction to reduce wind noise (which is a big problem with older Contour cameras at even moderate bicycling speeds), but the noise reduction also severely muffles your voice if you are trying to narrate a video while filming.

The camera controls are very easy to use, which is an improvement over earlier Contour cameras. The instant-on feature works great if you're filming only pieces of your event. I get about 3 hours of video from one battery charge. That also seems to be the amount of video that fits on a 32GB microSD card. If your event is longer than 3 hours, use the instant-on/instant-off feature to switch the camera on for just the important parts. The instant-on feature is a nice improvement over earlier Contour cameras that are difficult to turn on when you are moving.

Contour cameras seem to go on sale more often than GoPro. If you can catch it at a good sale price, I think Contour is a much better value than GoPro.
text_fidelity_b: ContourROAM Hands-free HD Camcorder

Amcrest 720P Wireless IP Camera WiFi Security Surveillance Camera System, HDSeries Indoor Camera for Baby Pet Nanny Monitor, Plug/Play, Pan/Tilt, Two-Way Audio & Night Vision IPM-721S (Silver) This item is a good choice IF you only want to install ONE SINGLE CAMERA. Multiple cameras drops you through a black hole into an alternate universe where nothing works or configures. I tried to install two of these over a period of four days and each time, some different and annoying glitch came up to prevent the things working as a system.

When installing two or more cameras and using WiFi as the way they're connected, each camera has to be located where the WiFi signal is strong or it will either not work or will respond slowly. This slow response is accompanied by ragged video images. Even installing a WiFi extender does not help, as the extender looks, and actually is, a different WiFi connection. To function together, and be viewed in side-by-side windows of the Amcrest View software, cameras MUST BE ON THE SAME CONNECTION.

In order to install the cameras, you need to download Amcrest View from the App Store (iPhones and iPads) or from Google Play (Android devices). The Lite version is free and wouldn't configure my cameras, nor did it provide the level of camera control I needed. I ended up purchasing the Amcrest View Pro app for $0.99 and even this did not allow me to successfully setup a dual camera system.

One of the cameras needed to be in a spot where WiFi was weak so I decided to link it up hardwired to the network. That requires using a tool from Amcrest called IP Config. I tried to install the IP Config software (supposedly on the CD that comes with the camera) and Windows promptly told me the folder was empty. I downloaded the install from the Amcrest website and the app ran but DID NOT install the IP config software on the computer. And, yes, I tried multiple times.

Several calls to tech support resulted in no useful resolution. Each tech told me something different. One, even wanted me to download and install a third-party app so he could take control of my PC. As he seemed to know very little about his subject matter and computing, I declined. The TECH SUPPORT IS AWFUL. After waiting in a long queue, I spoke to reps NOT IN THIS COUNTRY, who really did not understand my questions--a language issue--so they were of little use and just people in some other country doing a job that should be being done by someone living in, and contributing to the economy, of the United States.

I finally gave up on these cameras and sent them back. I will not ever purchase an Amcrest product of any sort again.

text_fidelity_a: Mighty Mule Wireless Driveway Alarm (FM231) At first I thought mine was faulty too.. we previously had a Mighty Mule driveway sensor that we loved and had for approximately two to three years before an ants nest took it over, plus damage from the weather killed it. So when that one went bad we went to Amazon to get the same model again because we loved the other one so much.. it arrived, we installed, and we kept getting faulty signals all hours of the day and night... to the point we would just unplug it at night. We attempted to call the customer service number and it was absolutely impossible to stay on hold for that length of time and not receive one person to talk to. I did the tech ticket online and did receive an email back after 2 days. That wasn't of much use. After a few tries my husband decided to turn the sensitivity down and bury the cable little bit deeper. I believe the manual says it needs to be around a foot when we only had at 6 to 7 inches..After digging a little deeper and turning the sensitivity down it seems to have done the trick. 64G Mp3 Player with Bluetooth, Mp4/Story Player, Music Player, Supports FM Radio of High Volume Built-in Speaker, 4-Inch LCD Full Touch Screen, E-Book, Micro SD Card Slot Ups to 512GB (Black) It does what it's sold to do very well. I've tested several types of ebooks (PDFs, epub, doc, txt), mp3 files of various quality, pics, and vids (avi, x264, and x265) - it read and ran everything well and smoothly.
Basically it's a low-end phone running an old distro of Android. It's super locked down and there's no internet access, so there's no updating and no adding of apps - this includes bluetooth tethering. That being said, a few of the apps are ones I've used for ages and (obv) I like them: specifically moon reader, the ebook reader - it really works well on this device. And I believe the video player is MX Player, also an old fav. Moving files via TF card was a bit of a pain, as the older version of android only supports up to 4GB at a time, but otherwise it moved everything without error. I tested the reader with several cards, from a generic 32gb to a samsung 512gb u3, and they all read well, so you can easily have a large library of media at hand. There's no cam or wifi; and there aren't any sensors, so it can't tell tilt, ambient light, etc. The screen is tiny but looks surprisingly good. The speaker is decently loud, but it def sounds like a phone speaker, still though, it's better than expected.
If you just want a simple media device with some neat features (FM works really well btw), this is great. I both would and wouldn't recommend this for kids - you can't add any educational apps (or games, lol), and they wouldn't be able to access things like their school portal or wiki; but if you only want your kid to have books, vids, and audio with a few tools (calc, calendar, alarm), this is right up your ally. Heads up though, they can swap out the TF card if they have a media collection you don't know about, and Moon Reader supports requiring passwords for opening the app.
If you want something you can do more with, I'd suggest foregoing the 50% off coupon and getting a burner phone at this device's list price. A burner probably won't work as smoothly (because it will have more hardware/software), but it'll have wifi and an app store and updates.
I plan to use this as an extra/backup media device. I'm one of those weird people that has a TF collection in my bag with tons of movies, tv, games, etc. I'm going to put one of those pockets on the back for credit cards, and use a TF card organizing card to hold my cards, so I'll have all my media together and with a device that can play them, in case my phone is AWOL or dead. IMO, after the coupon, it's worth the price as long as you know what you're getting.
text_fidelity_b: 64G Mp3 Player with Bluetooth, Mp4/Story Player, Music Player, Supports FM Radio of High Volume Built-in Speaker, 4-Inch LCD Full Touch Screen, E-Book, Micro SD Card Slot Ups to 512GB (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
WiFi Video Projector, WEWATCH V10B Wireless Portable Movie Projector with Bluetooth Full HD 1080P Supported Home Theater Video Projector Compatible with HDMI, VGA, TV Stick, iPhone, Android The WEWATCH V30 Portable Projector is a good 1080p projector for its size. I watched some movies with the screen setup to 80-90 inches and the picture looked very good in a dark room. It's important to watch this projector in low ambient lighting due to its low ANSI lumens, as bright light will wash out the picture.

The size of the projector is not as small as the pictures make it seem. Though it is not advertised as a pico projector, I expected it to be smaller. With that said, the projector is not so large that it would be hard to transport or store when not in use.

Unfortunately, I was not able to get the Wi-Fi feature to work with my Iphone. This is not a dealbreaker for me, as I plugged a Roku stick into the HDMI port and the system worked well.

I was surprised by how good the native speakers sound. I found watching movies enjoyable and voices were easy to hear. There are adjustments for the bass and treble levels in the menus. The unit has a headphone jack in the rear which makes hooking up an external speaker set up a breeze.

The fan on the unit is very quiet and is not distracting while it is in use.

While I really like this projector, there is a large downside. The lack of keystone correction is a huge oversight. Placing this projector without keystone adjustment means the projector has to be directly in line with the viewing area making it necessary to use a tripod in most instances. Having to bring a tripod along, makes the unit less portable.

Overall, this is a small projector with a great picture, as long as you can place it in the perfect location without much ambient lighting. If WEWATCH added keystone correction and refined the mirroring feature, this would be a 5 star projector.
text_fidelity_b: WiFi Video Projector, WEWATCH V10B Wireless Portable Movie Projector with Bluetooth Full HD 1080P Supported Home Theater Video Projector Compatible with HDMI, VGA, TV Stick, iPhone, Android

text_fidelity_a:
LeeKooLuu Backup Camera Rear View Monitor Kit HD 1080P for Car Truck Minivan Waterproof Night Vision DIY Grid Lines LK3 The camera and kit are a superb value. Installation was not difficult (including BOTH TIMES, I had to install the cable). Let me explain: When ordering it doesn't tell you what size cable comes with it, which is a 23 ft. cable. I found this out the hard and dirty way after a couple of hours on a winter Sunday afternoon painstakingly dragging myself underneath my truck; routing, securing, and cable-tying the camera cable from the back of my 2009 Ram 1500 (crew cab short bed) to the front, just to find out when I went to bring it through the firewall, I was about 5-7ft too short to reach the middle of my trucks console and mounting location. Pretty frustrating after spending hours to install and come up short. On re-reading the instructions by LKL they advised 'if cable too short, contact us for the longer 33ft. or 50ft cable'. Uhm OK, and I sent an email, and to their credit, they responded within a couple of hours asking for the size I wanted that would work. Unfortunately, a "short splicer" cable wasn't an option with both male finish end couplers on their cables to simply "Splice" into what was already routed 95% of the way already, so I asked for the 33ft. one. They sent it immediately, and I got it a few days later with plans to complete installation the following weekend from my original effort. So, new cable in hand I had to re-route the new cable basically starting over. A bit frustrating BUT hopefully this post will change their ordering system to ask "cable size" based upon application upfront; like for a car. SUV, truck, or RV. If, not simply message them ahead of time to install to see if they can send you a longer cable. not as efficient, but will save you the double-install time.

That said, I really like my camera. It has great clarity, good screen size, and detail. I like the flexible options for 16:9 vs. Narrower field, grid options and adjustments, etc. I also recommend adding LED back up lights to improve the night view of the camera which already includes some LEDs to help with night safety (you are likely reading this because you want better safety, and rearview vision, especially at night, correct?) You will already be removing one taillight assembly installing the splice-in to power the camera with the backup light wire, so you might as well install LED Backup bulbs both sides of the taillamp assembly.

I had a perfect spot in mind to install my camera in the center on top of my dash above the radio into a little "coin tray" recess. I had to snip about a half-inch off the camera holder base front and back to make it nestle in the bottom and adhere with the provided mounting tap securely. If I had it to do over again I likely would get their wireless camera product first, then see if the wireless signal worked OK given the length of the truck. (They don't recommend their wireless version for larger vehicles, like full-sized SUV's, trucks, or RV's but reviewers have reported satisfactory results with trucks and SUVs) Although it's a bit more $$ for wireless the amount of install time required for do-it-yourselfer's, or professional installation would be well worth it. If the wireless signal isn't good enough, return it since it wouldn't have been installed fully; then just order up this wired option. Good luck and happy backing up!
text_fidelity_b: LeeKooLuu Backup Camera Rear View Monitor Kit HD 1080P for Car Truck Minivan Waterproof Night Vision DIY Grid Lines LK3

text_fidelity_a: VIZIO M70-C3 70-Inch Class Ultra HD Full-Array LED Smart TV I really like this TV. So why 4 stars instead of 5? Well let me start with what is great about this TV and then we will get into why I dropped it a star. The price is amazing of course. I think back to the 42 inch Panasonic Plasma that I bought in 2002 and cringe at the multiple thousands spent. This is a lot of TV for the money. The picture is great. We have a 2012 59 inch top of the line Samsung Plasma and the picture on the Vizio is quite a bit sharper and brighter. It has replaced the Samsung as our go to Blue Ray movie night TV. So to this point we have a TV that is well priced and provides a great picture. So lets move on to the bad. Viewing angle. In our living room a couch sits directly in front of the Vizio. From the couch the picture is AMAZING. Off at about a 35 degree angle sits a recliner and the picture loses a lot of color, brightness and sharpness as viewed from the chair. It is not a horrible picture from the chair but it is quite a difference from straight on. The other is the somewhat slow response from the Vizio smart TV system. Compared to hooking up a Roku the initial start up and response is much slower. Of course if you are going to hook up a Roku then this is no big deal. If you do not have viewing angle concerns and are hooking up a Roku then I think you will absolutely love this amazing bargain.
text_fidelity_b: VIZIO M70-C3 70-Inch Class Ultra HD Full-Array LED Smart TV

Text is pretty blurry when you connect it to a computer as a monitor. If you do that, you might want to enlarge the font for readability.

Brightness is pretty good. It's better than mini projectors I've seen in the past. But the room (or outdoors, if you're using it there) will need to be pretty dark to get a good view. The farther away the projector is from the screen, the bigger the picture, the more spread out the light is, the darker the room will need to be to see it.

I had hopes the OS would play DVDs directly from a USB-powered outboard DVD player, but it doesn't have that functionality. I tried it and it would not recognize the connected device. You do have to manually select the input from the home screen. There are multiple inputs: HDMI, VGA, micro SD card, and USB.

The included screen is okay, but a white wall (or even ceiling) works well too.

On the bottom of the projector is a tripod mounting hole, a nice addition.

The manual keystone adjustment works only for up and down adjustment, not side to side. The focus is also manual, and works well.

The two negatives to me are that the remote control pretty much has to be aimed directly at the IR receiver ports on the projector to get it to work (there are ports on the front and back), and there is some trash inside the lens that shows up in the projected image in the one I received. I'll have to open up the projector to blow that out.

Other than that, at this price point, it's a good projector, and pretty versatile in terms of portability and input options.
text_fidelity_b: Luby Portable Movie Projector with Free Projector Screen Perfect for Fun Camping Neighborhood Gathering Backyard Movie

For outdoor activity, I cannot wear these. They fall out of my ear and I lose them. However, indoors I love the Alexa integration. As they work loose quickly, sound quality and volume diminishes. They do have good bass response when tightly fitted in your ear. If I am sitting still listening to music or an audio book, they work great. As I start to move around, they loosen up and sound poor and are at risk of falling out.

HP 1KF76AA#ABL OMEN by Wired Gaming Headset 800 (Black/Red) Bear in mind that as gaming headphones, the sound quality is not as suited for other applications like listening to music. Having said that, here's how the experience went:

Appearance: maybe this is some macho thing, but they are enormous and intense-looking in an almost exaggerated way. So if you're one of those people that likes huge flashy stuff or ostentatiously masculine-looking things, this is perfect? They're huge.

Comfort: Very comfy! The cup part is large and fits great, and the headband adjusts nicely to most average head sizes. The microphone is fully adjustable, making it work for anyone.

Sound blocking: pretty good! While it does not use noise-cancelling technology, the sheer size and generous build of the headphones allows for Very effective sound cancellation. I had my partner listen to something with her back to me so she could not see me, and with the volume turned up, I had to full on Scream for her to hear me.

Sound quality: Better for spoken word and voices, honestly. The sound is crisp and detailed, but it's also a little canned-sounding, with somewhat sharp, tinny trebles and less-than-intense bass. This does best in mid-range and capturing voices and sounds, and less so for actual music. Having said that, it is certainly better than cheap headphones for music, so it does have some versatility if you're not too picky.

Overall: These are pretty great! They even have an adapter that can be used by other devices that unites the audio input and output, which comes split for certain applications like computers or other gaming. (Meaning, theres a separate cable for the microphone and audio input, and they come with an adapter to have a single "female" connection that can work on phones or other single-plug devices using audio in/out.)

Headphone Adapter Converter Supports Audio and Charging for Motorola MotoZ, Letv ,2 in 1 USB-C to 3.5mm Audio Adapter, Nylon Braided 2 in 1 USB Type C Cable Fast Charge to 3.5mm Audio Jack(Black) This is a much easier alternative to the My K-cup option if you want to use your own coffee in a K-cup machine rather than the pre-packaged cups. Unlike the My K-cup you don't need to remove the inner cup of the machine to use this. It just drops right in, so you can switch between this and a regular k-cup without having to dismantle anything.

The kit is very complete. There are three cups, each a slightly different color (different shades of brown). The cups are decently made. The plastic sides are nice and thick; the o-ring on the cap is of good quality; and the metal mesh is firmly attached. My only quibble with the build quality is the hinge. It's plastic, and I don't have confidence that it will last a long time before breaking. It's not a big deal, since the cup will still work fine even with a broken hinge, so I'm not docking any points due to that potential problem.

I like that the water dispersion channel has slots all around it to ensure water gets sprayed in all directions inside the cup to keep the grounds uniformly wet. I also really like that the lip area has a slight indent to make it very easy to pop open the top with one hand.

It fit fine in my Cuisinart K-cup machine. The lid of the machine was just slightly raised compared with using a "real" k-cup, but it had zero impact on performance. I tried several different brews, all with good results. You will need to fiddle with the grind level to get the best coffee. Too fine of a grind and it gets over-extracted and bitter; too coarse and it's weak.

Cleaning a used cup is very easy. I pop open the top, hold it upside down in the compost pail, and whack it gently on the base with a wooden spoon. Nearly all the used grounds drop out, and what's left can be easily rinsed under running water. You can also just dump the contents into the disposal or garbage if you don't compost your grounds.

Another option is to use a mini filter in the cup. A package of them are included and, while they do make cleanup easier, I prefer to use just the cup without a filter.

The kit also includes a charcoal filter. I didn't use that, so I can't speak to its performance. It looks to be the same size as the filters used in the water intake of my Cuisinart K-cup machine, so I expect it would perform in a similar fashion.

This Smart Cup kit works well, is well-made/designed, and comes in a very complete kit. Having used the My K-cup version I can confidently say that this performs better and is easier to use. Highly recommend.
[Sample provided for review]

Young and broke, I saved and finally got a used triangle phone. By the way, in the movie 'The Birdcage', the receptionist is using one of the Bang & Olufsen banana phones. B&Os are in a lot of films.

It is true understated elegance.
The two shades of grey are exactly the 'right' shades. We all know what that means, it's like the difference between and on trend pleasing pink, and a Pepto-Bismol pink. The spun metallic is in a warm tone gives a more inviting feel to the set.

I do not expect these to sound like a $1,000 headset, if they were, I'd be slightly underwhelmed. But only slightly.
As far as dimension, the 3d effect, it's spectacular. The band or orchestra is right in front of you.
They pick up the nuance that other headphones miss. Funny story, I was listening to a song I've listened to a hundred times before, and heard some background that I had never heard before.

Just a heads up for those of us that wear red nail polish... I've taken these on and off so many times that little red streaks are starting to appear, as you can see in the photo. But you can also see how gorgeous these are.

Comments for WD PowerLine owners:
1. WD utility is unable to pickup on speed of the TP-Links (Rate Mbps). This is an application issue obviously and not completely sure if I can get around this as of yet.
2. I have not secured or modified network name as of yet which made things easier. Hope this does work when I get to it.
3. Ensure you have space for the bulky plug in unit. Not really an issue if you take the bottom wall plug.

My WD PowerLines were collecting dust until I moved. My previous home had a different circuit setup that prevented any PowerLine units from working correctly. They would see each other, but speeds were like dialup. So, don't be ticked if these do not work.

My new house has limited drops and roughly 3k Sq Ft over 2 floors and have no issues. My WD's have over 160 Mbps indicated on the utility from top to bottom.

ZAGG InvisibleShield HD – EZ Apply Film Screen Protector for Apple iPad Air/iPad Air 2 - Wet Apply, Clear TL;DR— not worth the extra cost, it will break and the lifetime warranty is a scam (website doesn’t work, always out of stock), just order a cheaper one and replace— IF you can somehow get Zagg to honor the warranty they will charge you at least $7 to send you a new one when this breaks (and it will def. break)

This was a great screen protector for the several months it lasted before cracking. That partially justifies the steep price tag compared to other screen protectors— but not really.

After I purchased this from amazon I registered this product on the Zagg website, which is necessary to potentially claim a replacement through the “lifetime” warranty program. When it broke, I logged back into their website to order a replacement. The first thing that was annoying was they had a message saying any product ordered within a several years long period would need to be re-registered after they had redesigned their website— my screen protector did not fall into this category, but I assume many people were out of luck on their warranties since they probably no longer had their receipts from screen protectors they had already registered. There was no email or anything warning consumers of this issue, although it’s possible it went out to only the affected people.

When I tried to order a replacement for my broken screen protector I got an error message telling me to try again later. Then the screen protector was out of stock. Then the website is down for maintenance. Then it was out of stock again. The Zagg screen protector on my phone is also broken and also had a warranty. Between the two I have been unable to order a replacement despite trying many, many times. I‘m not a computer engineer or anything, but my computer literacy is usually sufficient to navigate consumer websites. I’m pretty sure the issue is not with me, and if I am doing something wrong it’s because they have intentionally made their website impossible to navigate.

Eventually I gave up and just replaced the screen protector on my phone with a cheaper one. I was able to buy 2 new screen protectors for the same price as the SHIPPING for what the warranty replacement for the Zagg screen protector would have been if it was ever in stock when their website was working, and the difference in quality is negligible.

I don’t appreciate paying extra for a warranty that is not honored and having my time wasted trying to order a replacement when it’s clearly designed to be impossible. I also ended up keeping a broken screen protector on my phone and iPad for months while trying over and over again to order my replacement since it was under warranty.
text_fidelity_b: ZAGG InvisibleShield HD – EZ Apply Film Screen Protector for Apple iPad Air/iPad Air 2 - Wet Apply, Clear

Jawbone Big JAMBOX Wireless Bluetooth Speaker - Graphite Hex - Retail Packaging The first thing I noticed when I opened the box was how small the Big Jambox is. It's truly portable and the name is more accurate of its sound quality. The first thing I noticed when I turned on the unit was that it talked to me and charted out the steps to pair the speaker to the iPhone 5. The second thing I noticed was the sound. The big full sound. I have truly eclectic tastes. My music collection includes rock, blues, jazz, world music from Africa, the Middle East, and the Lapland of Norway. I listen to didgeridoos from Australia, fiddles, marimbas, and jaw harps from Kyrzykstan. The quality is so good Im a bit blown away by the technology. The clarity is a wonder when listening to vocal qualities of choir ensembles, Bobbie McFerrin, , solo clarinets, and horn sections as well as my favorite twangy African and Middle Eastern instruments. The bass is great considering the speakers size. I predict I will enjoy my symphonic classical music more from now on.
But be reasonable, put it in perspective. Don't expect your Big Jambox to take the place of the power of a live stadium U2 concert or the knock-you -on-your-ass sound wall that passes through your body from a live large brass section of a jazz band orchestra, or be loud enough to overwhelm 10 or 20 loud drunk party goers. Don't be a bonehead! It flabberghasts me that anyone would criticize this speaker. If you actually listen to the sound quality of singers and instruments, or enjoy deep full sounds, spend the money (im on the cheap side) and get the Big Jambox. And dats da facts Jack.

Amazon Basics Rolling Laptop Case, Black So I wanted to get some mileage on this bag before posting my review. I have had this bag now for almost 6 months and have used it regularly.
I like the overall design of the bag, it has held up nicely, wasn't super expensive and took the weight of a backpack off my back (so a plus for those of us who have back issues).

It has 3 zippered sections to put your things in. The first zippered section on the front has 2 pen pockets, 2 small pockets you can put pens or other things in, 4 business card pockets with a pocket the runs behind the business cards and 2 larger pockets that run horizontal behind all of that. (Ill include pictures to help show what I am saying)

The 2nd section has a laptop pouch. I measured my laptop and its length is 15 inches and is 10 inches wide/tall when in pouch, but it is a 17 inch screen (horizontal measurement of laptop for those who don't know). The pouch is has a little bit of padding on the front and back, so your laptop is safe there. The bottom seems okay as well and my computer has not suffered any damage, but for some who are more particular about their tech, you may want just a thin layer of foam or other cushioning (depending on the size of the laptop, you may can it in a sleeve into the pouch). There is also room to put some files or a binder in this section as well.

The last section is large enough to fit a 3 ring binder in, though you might fit a larger one if you don't have anything in the center section. The inside measurements are 13 inches tall from bottom to under the zipper and 15 inches wide from inside corner to inside corner. The dimensions listed in the product description say 17 (tall) x 14.5 (long) x 7.5 (wide)

Moving along to the wheels and handles. The wheels seem pretty sturdy so far and I have not had any trouble from them. They also are not swivel, so this may be a no go for someone looking for a bag with swivel wheels. The cloth handle is sturdy and nice to have when having to lift the bag out of your vehicle or going up stairs. The extended handle has a little loose feeling (and may feel cheap if you have owned a more expensive bag, but from my understanding of others reviews of more expensive bags, this seems to be a common complaint about the extend handles), but from my experience with it, it has served me well and has not given me any trouble. Also I am 5'5 and the handle is just right. My supervisor has the same bag and he is probably around 6'5 and the handle extends out far enough for him too.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Basics Rolling Laptop Case, Black

text_fidelity_a:
D-Link Pan & Tilt Wi-Fi Camera (DCS-5009L) (Discontinued by Manufacturer) This camera is yet another product made in China and sold here in the United States for prices equivalent to what we'd pay if the thing was actually made in the USA, which IT IS NOT. The plastic it's made with seems cheap and brittle.

The setup instructions are WRONG and can lead you through a lengthy hell to install and configure the camera. The camera DID NOT HAVE THE MOST CURRENT SOFTWARE and I was forced through an update TWICE because the first one was the wrong one. Yes, the wrong one was recommended on their website. It took a second pass to get the correct version. Speaking of their website, it's a real mess, difficult to navigate, impossible to locate what you need on it, and just plain annoying. Tech support is mostly via email and the one time I did get a human, he didn't know much about anything.

You may want to use the camera's web interface to set up security and so forth. The GOTCHA is the cameras use Java and Java is going to drive your internet security software, firewall and virus protection wild. Java is known to be a welcome mat announcing your computer is open for all manner of malware, virus infections and so on. My security software blocked the install entirely.

Access to the camera remotely is via the D-Link website through an account you set up. To see the camera's video you must go to the website, log in and then view the camera. As video goes from camera to the D-Link website and then to you via your mobile device, the panning and zooming is jerky due to the lag in the up and download of the signal.

If you're looking for a security camera to use while traveling, or out for an evening, this will take care of things--barely. If you want a home security system with multiple cameras, go for a dedicated system with hard-wired cameras, a DVR and a solid wall around it for security. This camera is a toy compared to industrial or home-grade security.
text_fidelity_b: D-Link Pan & Tilt Wi-Fi Camera (DCS-5009L) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
THINKWARE F550 Full HD Dash Cam with high-speed Cortex A8 Processor, GPS Tracker & Dual Save Technology I've tried some low-cost in-car cams and have been unimpressed with the build quality or video quality of the devices. The Thinkware 550 was a marked departure - it feels very well-built and solid. I'd rate the build quality up there with a decent conventional camcorder, such as a Sony. It also looks very attractive - they did a great job with the design.

This is not an "action cam" type of device for uploading videos of during stupid stuff onto Youtube (sorry, showing my age here - I probably would have done the same had cams been around in my youth). Rather, it's a cam for automatically documenting events that occur while driving (such as a crash or other incident) without any need for user action. Video files are time and date stamped, and assigned a location using GPS. It's more of a "black box" type recording device for a car rather than a "fun time" action cam with a car mount.

You can also use this while parked and with a rear camera, but both of those require additional items not included with this package (hard wire install for parking use; a separate camera for rear view use).

Installation is easy but also a little bit tricky. The mount is a plastic cradle with an adhesive backing. Once you determine where you want the cam mounted (up on the windshield is the recommended position) you peel off the backing on the adhesive pad and stick it to the windshield. It's a permanent mount (well, you can remove it from the glass, but it can't be reused). Easy to do, but tricky in that you really need to take some time before committing to a location and think through where the power cord needs to be routed.

The unit is lightweight (5.1 ounces without the cradle) and seems to be holding well to the windshield even over very bumpy terrain.. The manual suggests leaving the cam off the cradle until the adhesive has cured for 24 hours. I didn't see that tip until after I tested its holding ability over broken road. So if you miss that tip as well, it doesn't seem to be a problem.

The cam does not have a built-in battery. It must be powered by an included cigarette lighter adapter (known by "power ports" these days, but I still call them cigarette lighters). The adapter is very nicely made with a stout cord. That's good for longevity; not so good for routing it so the cord is not visible or in the way. There are some adhesive tabs included to lasso down the cable to help make for a neat (or semi-neat) install. I'll probably add some electrical tape to neaten up the install a bit more.

The manufacturer also cautions to make sure the power port you use gets shut off when you turn off the engine. The cam can continue to pull power if the power port is live, potentially draining your car's battery.

It automatically powers up when you start the car. It can be manually turned off (or back on) as well. It offers two recording modes: continuous (which is in one minute segments) or on-demand (you can manually start and stop). It also states that when there is an impact, the cam will store the 10 seconds before and the 10 seconds after in a secure memory folder. I'll have to take their word for that - can't really test that out! Under normal circumstances, when the micro SD card fills up it starts overwriting old files.

A micro SD card is included along with a reader. The card holds the user manual and the software, so it can't really be used to store video files. I used my own card reader rather than the one included since the included one was too tiny for my clumsy fingers to deal with.

There is no viewer on the cam - you have to take out the SD card and pull up the files using the included software. That for me is the biggest problem and limitation of this device. You have to trust that it's working since there's no confirmation other than the indicator lights and prompts. Nor can you set the camera specs unless you have access to a PC.

On the plus side, the lack of a screen means there's no risk of driver distraction while the cam is operating. I can't fault that. Still, I would have liked to see a design that has a screen that remains off until the camera is out of the mount so it can be used in-car to change settings or review stored video. That maintains the lack of driver distraction but still allows for better use of the cam while parked.

What makes up for a lot of these shortfalls is the video quality. Great - really great. Crisp, clear and sharp. It provides a panoramic view (the specs say 140 degrees) that easily covers the full view from the windshield. You really won't believe this is from a car cam. It dealt with head-on full sunlight pretty well, and did a decent job at night. I did get a fair amount of reflection off the windshield at night, but the video was very workable.

The included software installed fine on a Win 7 machine after I suspended Avast from running - this software does not want to work and play well with Avast. I even had to keep Avast suspended while running the software. Not tough to use - got the hang of it from just trying out menu options and playing around. It will ask to install an update right off the bat.

The video quality and overall "forget about it and it just records" type of operation are strong pluses. The power cord, mounting system, and lack of a view screen are problems. Weighing everything together gets me to a 3.5 star rating which I'll round up to 4 stars since the video quality is so nice. If you can live with the limitations, this is well worth considering.
text_fidelity_b: THINKWARE F550 Full HD Dash Cam with high-speed Cortex A8 Processor, GPS Tracker & Dual Save Technology

Brainwavz M1 in-Ear Noise Isolating Earphones While these don’t offer the sound quality of higher-end Brainwavz buds (or higher-end models from other brands), the sound quality and overall performance is quite good for the price point, and the comfort is excellent.

The best description I can offer of the sound quality is “clean.” The upper and mid ranges come through very clearly and are far more well-defined than typical with budget/value earbuds. The bass is not pronounced. It’s there, but it’s not what I’d describe as punchy. These are not an ideal set if you’re looking for head-thumping bass.

The comfort is typical for Brainwavz, which is to say it’s excellent. There’s a variety of ear tips so you can customize the fit to your ear. I’m especially fond of the Comply foam tips since they provide a great (but still comfortable) seal. That helps maintain good sound isolation and also helps with the bass response. It also helps keep the earbuds in place while exercising.

The cords are thin but seem sturdy enough for typical use. The same for the ear buds themselves. While they don’t have as solid of a build quality as higher-priced models, I don’t get the feeling that these will be falling apart anytime soon. That being said, it would have been nice to have more reinforcement where the cord meets the earbud, since that’s a prime stress point in use (even though these come with a very well made carry case, more often than not I just wind them around whatever device I am using).

For the price these are hard to beat. Highly recommend these as a not too expensive way to substantially upgrade from the stock earbuds that come with many devices.

text_fidelity_a:
LG 32GK850G-B 32" QHD Gaming Monitor with 144Hz Refresh Rate and NVIDIA G-Sync,Black Amazing monitor...

At 3000:1 the contrast is very nice and better than most at this price range, and essentially all TN/IPS.

This is why I like VA panels, the black levels and the contrast. I've always bought IPS before and they're still great obviously, but after having a VA television, I started to personally prefer its benefits. There are obviously a few downsides when it comes to VA monitors, but this particular model solves most of them.

I have 2 IPS displays on both sides of this, and I can tell you the colors look excellent. It was also close to perfect calibration right out of the box, which was a nice change.

One review mentioned Gamma Mode 1 as closer to 2.2, but another comment mentioned Gamma Mode 3. Mode 3 seemed closest to me when calibrating, so I would recommend it.

Viewing angles:

The viewing angles aren't very good, as expected, but it doesn't affect me as I'm always right in front of my monitors. There is some slight vignetting when sitting close, so a curved screen could have been nice if implemented well.

Backlight bleed:

Having no IPS glow or backlight bleed is another benefit. With larger VA tvs there can occasionally be some slight blobbiness when in very dark settings, but this panel is very uniform with no BLB that I can see.

Size/pixel density:

I personally love bigger monitors, and don't have an issue with the pixel density here. Some people who are more sensitive to that might not be completely satisfied, but I personally would choose the increased immersion of a larger panel. Regardless, 1440p is awesome.

Ghosting/input lag:

In terms of ghosting, it's surprisingly almost nonexistent. Here's some comments from other people:

"I played some Doom last night, and literally did nothing but rapidly move my camera all over the place to see if I could notice any ghosting or bleeding. I couldn't find anything objectionable..."

"Also there is very little ghosting in the monitor which is super rare for VA panels."

"...even in dark games like Outlast 2/Doom, the ghosting is so hard to see that you have to intentionally find a worst case scenario to try and induce it."

"Ghosting is slight, about on par with 165 Hz IPS gaming panels from my testing. Only TN is faster really."

In terms of input lag, tftcentral says: "We measured a total display lag of only 6.40ms. With approximately 4.15ms of that accounted for by pixel response times we had an estimated signal processing of just 2.25ms, which was next to nothing. This is in keeping with other G-sync screens we have tested, as the absence of an additional scaler (and presence of the G-sync module) allows for extremely low lag."

This monitor is exactly what I've been waiting for. The circular light bar on the back is a nice touch as well, although it could be a bit brighter. I also would have preferred a sharpness slider, but it's not entirely necessary.

FYI, it can be freely moved in basically every direction, including 90 degree rotation - if you need that for some reason.

So if you don't have issues with viewing angles/slightly higher pixel density, this is an excellent choice as it excels in basically every other area.
text_fidelity_b: LG 32GK850G-B 32" QHD Gaming Monitor with 144Hz Refresh Rate and NVIDIA G-Sync,Black
