text_fidelity_a:
Logitech Harmony Smart Control with Smartphone App and Simple All in One Remote - Black Build and Setup:
This is a very solid remote. Well constructed. It takes a disk watch type battery that is activated when you remove the tab. The lines are clean and elegant, and it feels well constructed.

Set up was very simple. I simply logged into myharmony.com and choose the Add a remote option.

The difference between this remote and other Harmony remotes is that this has a hub and blaster units that connects through your wireless network to allow you to connect and control your units with your smartphone.

You have to connect the hub and blaster unit around the units you want to control. It has to be connected to your home wireless network, which was easy. You can either do it through myharmony.com or by pressing the setup button on the hub and your router (if it supports it) it was that easy.

This particular unit controls my TV, Dish DVR, and VCR/DVD combo. Setting it up for the units was quite easy.

Using the Remote:
One selling point this has over the Ultimate is that the number buttons are solid state buttons, unlike the touch screen buttons on the Ultimate. As much as I like the touch screen technology, having buttons you can press by touch is a plus for.

There are also traditional DVR buttons, fast forward, as well as red, blue yellow, and green buttons. Since this remote did not have a 30 second advance button, and I rely on that, I programmed a short press of the green and yellow buttons to act as the skip forward. I programmed long pressing those buttons to do the default actions of those buttons. I appreciated that you could customize in that way.

Phone App:
The phone app for the android is a bit lacking as it is not quite as sophisticated as the remote itself, but can do most of the actions of the remote as long as you are connected to the same wireless network as your hub is.

Troubleshooting:
The remote is easy to use and troubleshoot, Simply rebooting or re-syncing the remote can resolve most problems I've found. It also prompts you for assistance the first time you add an action or new device.

Overall this is a great remote. This will demand, though, some knowledge on your part as it is a very sophisticated remote. Many problems that occur can easily be resolved by some knowledge of networks, remotes, or Harmony devices in general. If you have experience with this you will enjoy the functions and capacity of this remote.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Harmony Smart Control with Smartphone App and Simple All in One Remote - Black

1MORE iBFree In-Ear Earphones Wireless Headphones with Bluetooth 4.2 AAC, IPX 6 Waterproof, Secure Fit, In-Line Mic for Sports Gym Running - New Model Black I don't know what to think of these headphones. The sound out of the box is terrible, just abysmal. I've never heard a more unbalanced headphone anywhere. If you can't use an eq with these headphones, stop reading and look elsewhere.

If you can use an eq in your application, you might find these headphones surprising. Once the shrill high-end is toned down and the bass and mids bumped up, you will find the sound is pretty good for a ~$60/pair. The soundstage is small, but clear and the instrument separation surpasses what I was expecting. However, boost the bass too much and you will get distortion.

A couple of weeks before buying these I heard the quad-driver version and they were simply amazing. It was like I was sitting in my own living room listening to a full surround sound setup. I've never heard spacial definition or as big a soundstage in a headphone as I did with the quad-drivers, especially IEMs. The quad-drivers are on par with $600/pair HiFiMan planars. That's why I took a chance on this much cheaper bluetooth version of a single driver.

If you don't mind playing with the eq and don't want to buy cheap knock-offs from china (these are made in china, but by the company that designed them), take a chance on these. If you just want to plug and play, buy something else. I'm still on the fence on returning them myself.

text_fidelity_a:
Bose Noise Cancelling Wireless Bluetooth Headphones 700, with Alexa Voice Control, Soapstone Bose headphones are noise suppression first, sound fidelity second. If it’s sound fidelity you want, buy a comparably priced studio monitor headphone without noise suppression.

I’ve owned and worn out every iteration of the Bose noise-canceling headphones over the last 20 years for jet cabin noise suppression. Commercial airplane cabin noise is a proven travel fatigue-inducing component. A 2-17 hour flight with noise reduction headphones delivers noticeably less flight fatigue.

The QC-35’s are nearly worn out after another ‘million miles.’ They got 5 stars for the Bose attention to long-wear comfort. They’ve been beaten about, dinged, I’ve replaced the ear and head cushions twice. I suspect I have a wiring failure that’s about to reveal itself fully. I use the Bose most frequently without music for just the noise suppression. They work great as a sleep aid in hotels with and without music. Noise suppression is my #1 priority in this category. I have tested 2 of the latest Bose noise suppression headphone competitors. For several reasons, mostly head comfort and suppression extent, they still have a way to go to meet the Bose total experience.
The ambient noise suppression that these new 700 headphones provide is a significant improvement over the QC-35’s. The bass quality of Bose has always been a question mark easily revealed in a sales counter testing for comparison. Honestly, after an hour, the bass issue disappears in the Bose sound ambiance.

As to music reproduction, Bose does not represent the product as a monitor grade headphone. I happen to have a pair of Blue Ella monitor grade headphones. It is an error to compare the Bose work-horse noise suppression headphones that the 700 series represent with studio monitor grade fidelity. There is no question that studio monitor grade headphones deliver superior fidelity for the time they are worn.

Can I comfortably wear the Blue Ella’s on a trans-con flight? No (plus they are prone to a five-finger discount). They simply aren’t designed for hours of head comfort. The Blue Ella’s are fantastic for a couple of hours but are no way suitably head comfortable for a 17-hour flight to Australia.

The Bose 700’s are a clear step up for the QC-35 users. These are lighter on the head, and though they don’t have hingey elements of the QC-35, I’ve not experienced a flexibility problem from this lighter weight and flexible design. They are an improvement in the Bose reputation for the best designed, long-wear consideration.
text_fidelity_b: Bose Noise Cancelling Wireless Bluetooth Headphones 700, with Alexa Voice Control, Soapstone

LENRUE Portable Wireless Bluetooth Speaker with Built-in-Mic,Handsfree Call,AUX Line,TF Card for iPhone Ipad Android Smartphone and More (Grey) I've been wanting my own bluetooth speaker forever. The interesting thing is that I'm not even interested in the bluetooth capability. I want the aux connection for my first generation iPod, which doesn't have bluetooth technology. My iPhone just doesn't have the space for all the music I have on the iPod, plus I don't want to use up data streaming Pandora. Additionally, bluetooth and getting stuff to connect is just a pain. So, I've never tried to connect via bluetooth only the aux.

At first I thought I had dud. I charged it and went to push the power button and nothing happened. I read the tiny print in the instructions and still nothing. So, I went on YouTube to see if anyone made video about using this and of course there is! So, you have to press the power button until the device glows blue and beeps! No where on the instructions does it say to do this! So, once you do this, then you can follow the directions to use the speaker. If you are going to just use the aux plug then push the "M" button, which I think stands for mode. You're good to go.

Now this is tiny, so you're going to get a lot of output, but it what it does put out is a decent sound. I have used mine in a small pavilion for a party and on my front porch. At the party depending on the song, a few downloaded from the early aughts were too quiet to hear, but songs downloaded from iTunes or from CDs came out loud enough to hear throughout the pavilion. Just make sure the volume is up on your speaker AND your device. I've used for about 12 hours total. 4 hours here, 4 hours there, etc., and I still haven't charged it. So it holds a good charge to last through a party or an afternoon lounging on the porch.

You get an aux cord and a USB charging cord. So you can charge it on the computer or with a charger plug that uses a USB plug. The light ring turns red when charging and goes off when it's fully charged. The ring glows blue when it is on. It flashes when it it searching or looking for a bluetooth device. I bought this after a family member refused to let me use his "expensive someone is going to steal it" bluetooth speaker even though he never uses it (and I'm never in a situation to have someone steal it.)
text_fidelity_b: LENRUE Portable Wireless Bluetooth Speaker with Built-in-Mic,Handsfree Call,AUX Line,TF Card for iPhone Ipad Android Smartphone and More (Grey)
